name: web-research
label: Web research

tools.name: search
tools.use: Search the web and read the top results. Prints a numbered list plus the text of the top 3 pages, so one call usually answers the question.
tools.args: The query as plain words — no quote characters, they become part of it. --read N reads that many pages instead of 3, --read 0 gives links only. --recent day|week|month|year limits by age and is what you want for news. -n N sets list length (default 6). --site DOMAIN restricts to one domain, --region CODE biases to one (uk-en, us-en).
example: best local model for tool calling

tools.name: fetch
tools.use: Read web pages as markdown — headings, lists, tables, code and links kept, navigation and markup discarded.
tools.args: One or more URLs. --max-chars 0 removes the 24,000-character cap, --save DIR also writes each page to a file, --links prints the page's links instead of its text.

tools.name: doc
tools.use: Read a file as text — PDF, Word, Excel, PowerPoint, an image, or anything text. This is how you open a file someone attached: attachments arrive as a path under uploads/ and are the one thing you cannot see without opening.
tools.args: One or more file paths. A scanned PDF or a photo of text is read with OCR automatically — add --lang deu (or fra, spa, ita, por, nld, rus, ukr, swe, nor, dan, fin) when it is not English. --max-chars 0 removes the 24,000-character cap, --save DIR also writes the text out.

tools.name: tools
tools.use: Print this toolbox's reference — every command, its flags, and worked examples.
tools.args: Nothing for all of it, or a section name: search, fetch, doc, files, pdf, limits, recipes.

tools.name: rg
tools.use: Search inside files you already saved to the workspace.
tools.args: A pattern and a path, relative to the workspace. -n prints line numbers, -i ignores case.

tools.name: jq
tools.use: Filter or reshape JSON, usually from curl.
tools.args: A jq filter, then a file — or nothing after it to read stdin.

tools.name: curl
tools.use: Call an API, when you want the raw bytes rather than a page to read.
tools.args: -sSL and a URL. Use fetch for anything you intend to read as text.

tools.name: python3
tools.use: Run Python, for anything the other commands cannot express.
tools.args: -c and a program, or a script path. requests, lxml, beautifulsoup4, trafilatura, python-docx, openpyxl, python-pptx and Pillow are installed.

notes: Run `tools` for the full reference with worked examples. `search` already reads the top results for you, so answer from that page text rather than from the snippets — and one search is usually enough: if it did not answer the question, `fetch` one of the URLs it gave you for the full page instead of searching again with different words. There is no browser and no JavaScript engine, so a page that renders client-side comes back empty and says so. Use `doc` on a file the user attached — those arrive as a path under uploads/, and for a PDF, a spreadsheet or a scan the path is all you are given. Paths are the same ones the file tools use: write `uploads/report.pdf`, not an absolute path. Write findings to the workspace and search them with rg rather than holding whole pages in context.
